privacy_collect_heading: Information we collect and how we use it
privacy_collect_contact: The name, email address, and message we receive in an inquiry email are used only to reply to and handle that inquiry.
privacy_collect_access: When you view the Site, cookies and similar technologies automatically collect information such as the pages you view, the referrer, your approximate region, and the type of device and browser you use. We use this for access analytics and for displaying ads, and not to identify any specific individual.

privacy_cookie_body: Cookies are small pieces of data stored in your browser. On the Site, the Google services listed below use cookies. You can disable or delete cookies in your browser settings. You can still view the Site with cookies disabled, but some features may not work properly.
privacy_external_intro: For the services below, the Site sends information from the visitor's browser to external companies (disclosed under Article 27-12 of the Telecommunications Business Act of Japan).
privacy_ga_data: The URL and title of the pages you view, the referrer (including source information attached to links such as ad QR codes), the date and time of viewing, your approximate region estimated from your IP address, the type of device, OS, and browser, your screen size, an identifier stored in a cookie, and your actions on the Site (such as clicks on the contact links)
privacy_ga_purpose: To understand how the Site is used and help improve its content and operation
privacy_ga_optout: You can stop data from being sent to Google Analytics by installing the Google Analytics Opt-out Browser Add-on in your browser.
privacy_adsense_data: The URL of the pages you view, the referrer, the date and time of viewing, your IP address, the type of device, OS, and browser, and an identifier stored in a cookie

privacy_google_partner: How Google uses information it receives from partner sites is explained in "How Google uses information from sites or apps that use our services."
privacy_contact_body: For questions about this policy and how information is handled, please write to the email address below.
privacy_changes_body: We may revise this policy to reflect changes in law or in how the Site is run. Revisions take effect when they are posted on this page.

pn_meta_title: promptnotes — A local notes app for writing prompts before you send them to AI
pn_hero_subtitle: A local notes app for writing prompts before you send them to AI.
pn_download_note_other: promptnotes runs on macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux.
pn_download_note_failed: Couldn't get the latest version info. Please download it from the releases page on GitHub.
pn_download_other_os: Download for other OSes and formats
pn_screenshot_alt: The promptnotes window, with saved prompt notes listed from newest to oldest
pn_problem_body: In Claude Code and Codex, pressing Enter while you're typing a prompt sends it to the AI right away. Have you ever pressed Enter for a new line and sent a prompt you hadn't finished?
pn_solution_heading: Enter adds a new line. Send only when you're done
pn_solution_enter_body: promptnotes is an editor for writing prompts before you send them to AI. Pressing Enter never sends anything.
pn_solution_shortcut_body: To send, press Cmd+Enter (Ctrl+Enter on Linux). It's a different key combination from Enter, so you won't press it by accident.
pn_solution_local_body: Every note is saved on your computer as a .md file. You can open them in other editors and tools, and take your data wherever you like.
pn_feature_markdown_body: Syntax highlighting powered by CodeMirror 6, plus list and bracket completion.
pn_feature_search_body: Search note text and tags in real time. Press Cmd+F (Ctrl+F) to jump straight to the search box.
pn_feature_tags_body: Add tags to your notes and click one to filter by it.
pn_feature_copy_body: Copy just the note text to the clipboard, without the frontmatter or tags.
pn_feature_autosave_body: Your note is saved to its .md file automatically 0.5 seconds after you stop typing.
pn_feature_filter_body: Filter by the last 7, 30, or 90 days or show everything, and sort by date created or date modified.
pn_install_intro: The macOS version isn't notarized by Apple, so Gatekeeper shows a warning the first time you open it. Open it using one of the methods below.
pn_install_a_heading: Method A: Allow it in System Settings (macOS 15 Sequoia and later)
pn_install_a_lead: On macOS 15 and later, choosing Open from the right-click menu doesn't get you past the warning.
pn_install_a_step1: Move promptnotes.app to the Applications folder and double-click it to open it. When a "Not Opened" dialog appears, click Done (clicking Move to Trash deletes the app).
pn_install_a_step2: Open System Settings, go to Privacy & Security, scroll down to the Security section, and click Open Anyway.
pn_install_a_step3: Authenticate with your administrator password (or Touch ID).
pn_install_a_step4: Open promptnotes.app again. If a confirmation dialog appears, click Open Anyway there as well.
pn_install_a_legacy: On macOS 14 Sonoma and earlier, you can also start it by right-clicking (or Control-clicking) promptnotes.app in Finder, choosing Open, and then clicking Open in the warning that appears again.
pn_install_b_heading: Method B: Remove the attribute in Terminal
pn_install_b_body: If you still see "is damaged and can't be opened" after trying Method A, run the following command in Terminal. After that, the app opens without a warning.
pn_platforms_nix: If you use Nix (flakes), you can run it with the following command.
pn_platforms_unsupported: Intel Macs aren't supported. Windows support is planned.
pn_behind_body: How promptnotes was built (how I chose the tech stack, how I worked with ori, my own framework, and what was hard) is covered in WORKS.
